title: Quantification of Total Biomass in Ground Coral Samples
author: Rowan McLachlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdyai7se
materials: Prepare equipment for grinding corals. Prepare a mortar and pestle within an ice bath (Fig. 2). Mortar and pestle can additionally be chilled using liquid nitrogen or by placing in -80 °C freezer ~20 minutes prior to use. Fig. 2. Equipment used for grinding coral fragments into a homogenous paste.

steps.title: Label Weighing Pan A
steps.instruction: Engrave the base of a pre-baked aluminum weighing pan (Pan A) with the coral sample ID using an unleaded mechanical pencil.

steps.title: Grind Frozen Coral Fragments
steps.instruction: Rapidly grind a coral fragment from the -80 °C freezer into a homogenous paste in a mortar to prevent defrosting and degradation (complete process in ≤ 5 minutes).

substeps.instruction: Place the coral fragment in the mortar.
Use a pestle to break the fragment into ~1 cm 3 pieces, covering the mortar with one hand to prevent ejection.
Continue crushing the pieces into smaller fragments.
Use circular movements to grind the coral into a homogenous paste resembling hummus.
Gather all coral paste at the base of the mortar using the pestle.

steps.title: Tare Balance with Pan B
steps.instruction: Prepare the balance and a second pre-baked aluminum weighing pan (Pan B) for weighing.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the weighing balance and zero it.
Place Pan B on the balance and tare.

steps.title: Transfer and Weigh Ground Coral Paste
steps.instruction: Transfer the ground coral paste from the mortar to Pan B and record the initial wet weight.

substeps.instruction: Remove Pan B from the balance and place it on the workbench.
Use a plastic spatula to scrape all ground coral paste from the mortar and pestle into Pan B.
Place Pan B back on the balance and record the total wet weight (grams) in Excel.

steps.title: Partition Biomass Sub-sample
steps.instruction: Transfer a small portion of the paste to Pan A and determine the exact weight of the sub-sample.

substeps.instruction: Use a metal spatula to transfer ~1 g of ground coral paste from Pan B into Pan A.
Spread the material into a thin layer within Pan A using the metal spatula.
Re-weigh Pan B and record the post-partitioning wet weight (grams) in Excel.
Calculate the subsample wet weight (g) = Total wet weight (g) - Post-partitioning wet weight (g).

steps.title: Dry and Weigh Samples
steps.instruction: Dry the sub-sample and a control pan, then record their dry weights.

substeps.instruction: Place Pan A (with sub-sample) and an empty pre-baked pan (control) into a 60 °C drying oven overnight.
Remove pans and allow them to cool on a workbench.
Weigh each pan in triplicate, taring the balance between measurements.
If a pan's weight does not stabilize after 1 minute (mass continues to drop), remove it and cool for an additional 5 minutes.

steps.title: Burn and Weigh Samples
steps.instruction: Burn the dried samples in a muffle furnace and record the final weights to determine Ash-Free Dry Weight (AFDW).

substeps.instruction: Load Pan A and the control pan into a muffle furnace and burn for 6 hours at 450 °C.
Remove pans and allow them to cool on a workbench.
Weigh each pan in triplicate, taring the balance between measurements.

Calculate AFDW (g) using: Δ Coral weight (g) = average weight dry coral pan (g) – average weight burnt coral pan (g); Δ Control weight (g) = average weight dry control pan (g) – average weight burnt control pan (g); AFDW (g) = Δ Coral weight (g) – Δ Control weight (g).

steps.title: Archive Remaining Coral Paste
steps.instruction: Store the remaining material from Pan B for future analysis.

substeps.instruction: Bend Pan B to create a pouring spout and pour any liquid into a pre-labeled 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Use a plastic spatula to scrape the remaining coral material into the centrifuge tube until the pan is empty.
Cap the tube and return it to the -80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Calculate Final Biomass
steps.instruction: Standardize the AFDW to the surface area of the sub-sample to determine biomass.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the surface area of the sub-sample: SA subsample (cm 2 ) = [Subsample wet weight (g) ÷ Total wet weight (g)] x SA whole colony (cm 2 ).
Calculate biomass: Biomass (g / cm 2 ) = AFDW (g) ÷ SA subsample (cm 2 ).
